name: Amala with Ewedu and Gbegiri
summary: Dark yam flour dough served with slippery jute leaf soup, velvety bean soup and a spicy stew.
story: Amala is a Yoruba staple made from yam flour (elubo), and is often eaten with ewedu, gbegiri and a spicy stew, a combination known as abula. It is a favourite in homes and amala restaurants across south-western Nigeria. Many people enjoy it for lunch or at gatherings.

steps.title: Cook the beans
steps.text: Boil the peeled beans in plenty of water for 40 to 50 minutes until they collapse when pressed. Add more water if it runs low.

steps.title: Blend gbegiri
steps.text: Blend the beans until completely smooth, return to the pot, and simmer with palm oil, crayfish, onion and salt for 10 minutes, stirring, until velvety.

steps.title: Cook ewedu
steps.text: Boil 2 cups water with a pinch of potash, add the leaves and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until very soft and dark green.

steps.title: Mash ewedu
steps.text: Use a wooden ewedu whisk or blender to mash the leaves into a smooth, slippery soup. Add iru and salt and simmer for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Warm the stew
steps.text: Reheat the stew gently until bubbling and the oil rises on top. Taste and adjust salt.

steps.title: Make the amala
steps.text: Bring 2 cups of water to a boil. Sprinkle in flour while stirring quickly to prevent lumps, then lower the heat and cover for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Beat the dough
steps.text: Turn with a wooden spoon, adding the rest of the water in splashes, and beat firmly for 5 to 7 minutes until smooth, dark and elastic.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Shape into balls and serve with ewedu, gbegiri and stew in separate bowls so each can be spooned over.

tips: Pour the flour in gradually and stir fast; this prevents lumps.
Peeled beans make gbegiri smoother and lighter in colour.
A small pinch of potash helps the ewedu break down but too much tastes soapy.

swaps.swap: Frozen jute (molokhia) from Middle Eastern or African shops is a good match.
Cassava flour or plantain flour can make amala, with different colour and taste.
